scores.reasoning: The father's decision to 'bring up the child or to expose it' concerns the survival/death of the infant.
The mention of whether an offspring should be 'cared for and not put away' or 'exposed' relates to the right to life.
Refers to litigants in a suit restricted by the 'water-clock' and the 'brief' (affidavit) from which no deviation is allowed.
Describes arguments 'persuasive in court' and the ability to give a professional opinion for a fee.
The verbatim discusses a man who 'bought a cloak' and had it under his 'control' or 'possessed' it.
Refers to the 'profession of those who are... called orators' and their power to 'persuade men'.
Refers to 'judges' (dikastai) being persuaded and passing 'judgement' based on evidence or hearsay.
Describes the intensity of 'bodily sufferings' and physical 'pleasure' in a diseased versus healthy state.
Discusses those who are 'laughed at' and whether such ignorance is considered 'ridiculous' or 'infamous'.
Contrasts the 'arithmetic of the people' with that of 'philosophers' regarding accuracy in truth and measures.
Discusses degrees of 'certainty' and 'guesswork' in professional arts like medicine and generalship.
Refers to a rule to 'refrain from loving our freeborn women,' implying protection from unsolicited advances/outrage.
Fathers put tutors in charge of boys to 'prevent them from conversing with their lovers,' a restriction on movement/association.
States that these men alone 'prove in a public career to be men,' identifying access to high office.
Agreements 'willingly made are held to be just' by the 'sovereign, the law,' implying judicial recognition of contracts.
Describes men having 'no natural interest in wiving' but doing so only 'under stress of custom'.
Concerns 'priestcraft concerning sacrifice and ritual' and the 'converse of men with gods'.
Discusses the biological 'yearning to beget' and the 'conjunction of man and woman'.
Mentions that in the name of legislators like Lycurgus and Solon 'has many a shrine been reared' as an honor.
Describes the 'right method' of ascending from 'beautiful bodies' to 'beautiful learning'.
